equation_title: the paper's equation, with tighter bounds
equation_caption: The same equation as the paper's: a baseline plus two independent peaks, each a generalized Gaussian with its own centre, its own left and right widths and its own exponent p. The only differences are the ranges the program allows: p between 0.5 and 4 (the paper's floor is 0.1), widths at least 0.06 radians, and amplitudes at most 100.
equation_html:
Paper's equation (11 parameters): f(θ) = b + A₁ exp[−½ (|θ−φ₁| / σ₁±)p₁] + A₂ exp[−½ (|θ−φ₂| / σ₂±)p₂]
This run's winner (11 parameters): f(θ) = b + A₁ exp[−½ (|θ−φ₁| / σ₁±)p₁] + A₂ exp[−½ (|θ−φ₂| / σ₂±)p₂], 0.5 ≤ p ≤ 4
caveats: Stopped at the spend cap. The run reached its $9.50 cap (list price; billed to the OpenCode Go allowance) after 8 of 12 generations. Upstream writes its program databases only at the end, so they were rebuilt from its log and last census with edgar recover; every program's code matched its logged translation. Upstream's own final evaluation never ran. The candidate pool is every program it had scored, including ones a finished run would have pruned from its islands, so it is larger than run 219bfc's.

The paper's form from the first generation. 11 of the 44 generation-0 programs already had two free peaks, separate left and right widths and an exponent, and the winner has exactly the paper's 11 parameters. No program mentions the paper, and each explains every term from the plotted neurons. But this model was not asked directly whether it knows the paper, because that call would have gone past the spend cap, so recall cannot be ruled out (docs/LEAKAGE.md).

Peakiness close to the paper's. Across all 2,110 reliable neurons the median min(p₁, p₂) is 1.19 against the paper's 1.20, and only 3% of the locked-test neurons sit at the floor of 0.5. The free run's winner, with a floor of 1, has about half of its locked-test neurons there.

α does not match the paper's numbers. The winner gives α ≈ 3.6 (log fit), between the paper's equation refitted here (3.4) and the double Gaussian (4.4). As for the other run, the paper's own values (4.34 for its equation, 4.26 for the data) are not reproduced on this recording; see that run's caveat.
Reasoning effort. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash has no non-thinking mode, so routine calls used effort low where upstream used non-thinking Gemini 2.0 models.
Different fitter. Candidates are fitted with bounded Levenberg–Marquardt instead of upstream's Adam; scores agree to within about 0.7%.

differences.summary: The same equation as the paper's, term for term, with two independent peak centres instead of an offset; that is the same thing written differently. Only the allowed ranges differ.

rows.paper: amplitude A₁ ≥ 0 at the preferred direction φ
amplitude A₂ ≥ 0, centred anywhere: opposite φ, shifted by up to ±180°
rows.winner: its own centre anywhere on the circle, the same freedom written as a second angle

rows.paper: separate left and right width for each peak (4), each at least 0.01 rad
rows.winner: same, each between 0.06 and π rad

rows.paper: one exponent per peak (2), between 0.1 and 10
rows.winner: one exponent per peak, between 0.5 and 4
